quizData.question: Which keyword is used in Java to establish single class inheritance, and what class does every class implicitly extend if none is specified?
In what order are constructors executed when an object of a derived subclass (`FirstYear` extends `Student` extends `Person`) is instantiated?
quizData.answer: Person -> Student -> FirstYear (Parent constructors execute before child constructors)
choices: Person -> Student -> FirstYear (Parent constructors execute before child constructors)
FirstYear -> Student -> Person (Child constructor executes first)

quizData.question: What is the difference between Static Polymorphism and Dynamic Polymorphism in Java?
quizData.answer: Static polymorphism is resolved at compile time via method overloading, while dynamic polymorphism is resolved at runtime via method overriding.
choices: Static polymorphism is resolved at compile time via method overloading, while dynamic polymorphism is resolved at runtime via method overriding.
Static polymorphism uses `abstract` classes, while dynamic polymorphism uses `final` classes.
Static polymorphism requires interfaces, while dynamic polymorphism requires packages.
Dynamic polymorphism cannot be used with subclasses.

quizData.question: Which of the following is a strict rule when overriding a method in a subclass?
quizData.answer: The overriding method in the child class must be at least as accessible (not more restrictive) and cannot throw new or broader checked exceptions.
choices: The overriding method in the child class must be at least as accessible (not more restrictive) and cannot throw new or broader checked exceptions.
The overriding method must be declared `private`.
The overriding method must have a different return type.
The overriding method can throw any checked exception regardless of the parent method.

quizData.question: Can a class declared with the `final` keyword (e.g., `final class SecurityManager`) be extended by another class in Java?
quizData.answer: No, a final class cannot be extended or inherited.
choices: No, a final class cannot be extended or inherited.
Yes, by using the super keyword.
Yes, if in the same package.
Yes, but only by abstract classes.
